doctrine: The policy lives BELOW the frozen seam: the session service still calls ONE RealtimeRail, the port's shapes and the admission ordering (POLICY → CAPABILITY → BUDGET → SECRET MEDIATION → adapter) are untouched, and no failure is ever masked — non-retryable failures never re-bind.

designDecisions.decision: the preference order derives from the EXISTING materialization gates (zero new environment variables, zero manifest changes): the LiveKit set materializes ⇒ PREFERRED (PPR-009's primary); the socket.io set ⇒ ALTERNATE (PPR-010's alternate); only-socket.io ⇒ the alternate stands alone as the preferred; NOTHING materializes ⇒ EXACTLY today's simulated terminal fallback (the in-process rail, no policy in effect — rebinds is empty forever, pinned both ways)

the ONE-rebind bound is structural: each openSession invocation starts at the standing preferred and may hop to the alternate AT MOST ONCE (only when a MATERIALIZED alternate exists — the unmaterialized gate's simulated rail is NEVER a failover target, because substituting a fake for a dead real rail would mask the capacity event); when the alternate also fails, its normalized PlatformError surfaces with the preferred's failure retained as the cause (code/message/retryability pass through unchanged)

the re-bind trigger is the RETRYABLE NORMALIZED failure only (a PlatformError with retryable=true — the neutral failure vocabulary both real rails normalize onto); authentication, not-found, upstream-error and every non-normalized escape NEVER re-bind (an auth failure is not a capacity event); the SAME request object — the same coordinates, the same stable rail-level idempotency key — reaches the alternate (the drilled convergence: exactly-once PER RAIL, never cross-rail dedupe)

NO MID-SESSION FLAPPING: a session lives on the rail that opened it — deliverTurn/transferCall/closeSession route through a per-session in-memory affinity record (the channelSessionRef the open returned → the rail that produced it); only openSession may re-bind, and every new open starts at the standing preference (per-invocation, never sticky — a recovered preferred is retried); the composed rail's descriptor names the rail that served the most recent successful open (the standing preferred before any open) — the serving rail's own railCapabilityId IS the honest disclosure, zero port-shape changes; per-session truth is observable through the binding-level servedBy()/rebinds() accessors in the same neutral vocabulary

the honest in-memory-affinity boundary: a frame for a channelSessionRef this process never opened (post-crash recovery of a session a previous process re-bound) routes to the STANDING PREFERRED rail and fails neutrally there if the preferred never saw that ref; the durable cross-rail ledger that would close this boundary is PPR-009's recorded residual, unchanged by this order

the composition wiring point, recorded honestly: NO composition consumer binds a realtime rail today (deploy/api.ts wires no RealtimeRail — surveyed for bindEnvironmentRealtimeRail/bindEnvironmentSocketIoRail/RealtimeRail: zero matches); the binding ships through the additive barrel exports (adapters/index.ts + deployments/public.ts, value imports wired) ready for the composition root, mirroring the existing gates' wiring pattern

an empirical finding from the drill's development, recorded honestly: a SIGSTOP-frozen-but-listening livekit upstream turns the bounded request timeout into a TimeoutError that normalizes as upstream-error — NON-retryable — and the policy CORRECTLY never re-binds on it; the drill's refusal injection therefore TERMINATES the server (connection refused ⇒ the neutral unreachable class, retryable), which is also the more honest model of a capacity event

no mid-session flapping: after a re-bind, session one's deliver/transfer/close STILL follow the rail that opened it (the stubs' frame records prove the routing), session two's follow the alternate, and a frame for a never-opened ref follows the STANDING preferred (the in-memory-affinity boundary)
